task_description: We need to extract our authentication module out of the Rails monolith into its own service. Auth is currently baked into the main app alongside billing and document logic. We had a 40-minute auth outage last year when a schema change broke session lookup and our deploy and rollback got out of sync. I want to do this right. We have 8,000 active users and 3 enterprise SAML customers who cannot have downtime.
context:
## Current System

Single Rails monolith on Heroku. PostgreSQL + Redis. Auth uses Devise + OmniAuth (Google) + SAML for enterprise. Sessions are cookie-based. Auth models (User, Team, Membership, SamlConfiguration) live alongside all other app models. The team is 4 engineers.

## What We Want

Move auth logic to a separate service. Long-term: swap in a managed auth provider (Clerk or WorkOS). Immediate need: mobile app launching in Q3 needs token-based auth, which is blocked on extracting sessions from the monolith.

## Our Concerns

- The schema migration / deploy desync that caused the last outage
- SAML enterprise customers need zero downtime
- No test coverage around session middleware or role-checking logic

task_description: Our order service writes a structured log field called `usr` that our internal dashboards query. We want to rename it to `user_id` for consistency with every other service. Nothing customer-facing reads these logs, and the dashboards are ours. I'd like a quick plan so this doesn't surprise anyone.
context:
## Current System

Order service (TypeScript) emitting JSON logs to the team's log platform. Two internal dashboards and one saved alert query use `usr`. Deploys go through CI with a canary stage and one-click rollback to the previous release. There is a unit test asserting the log line's shape.

## Constraints

- Log retention is 30 days; dashboards query the last 7 days
- The team owns all three consumers of the field

1.0=assigns LOW: severity is None or Degraded (internal dashboards only), rollback is a one-click release revert, nothing is removed, the shape test covers the field; says the user can approve or tell the agent to go ahead (recorded as delegated) and that CI and code review are the gate; 0.5=assigns moderate with a reasonable rationale, or low with no rationale; 0.0=assigns high, or adds review ceremony (named reviewer, extra approvals) to this change, or no tier
